name: Accessibility tester with lived disability experience (Fable)
summary: Toronto-founded company that pays people with disabilities who use assistive technology to test websites and apps for accessibility.
whatYouDo: You complete testing tasks on client websites and apps using the assistive technology you already rely on (e.g. screen reader, magnification, alternative input) and give feedback. You choose how much to work each month.
appeal: Residents of Canada, the US and the UK are eligible (official)
Values lived experience with assistive technology over formal credentials
Paid training and a 'competitive hourly wage'; Fable says testers average more than double minimum wage
Credible: a Government of Canada notice named Fable as the only provider of this kind of tester pool
watchOuts: Only for adults with vision, mobility or cognitive accessibility needs, including daily assistive-technology users
Exact hourly rate not published in what we saw
Contractor status, paid once a month in arrears
Onboarding includes an assistive-technology and communication-skills assessment and a conversation with staff

training.notes: Testers complete paid training after the assessment.

compensation.notes: Fable describes a 'competitive hourly wage' and says testers earn on average more than double minimum wage; no figure published in what we saw. Paid at month-end.

reliability.notes: Testers choose how much to work monthly; available volume not published. A 2020 figure cited about 100 testers.

applicationSteps: Sign up on Fable's community page and verify your email
Describe the assistive technology you use
Talk with a Fable team member and complete the AT and communication skills assessment
Complete paid training, then take testing tasks
fitsIf: You are an experienced assistive-technology user in Canada who wants flexible, fairly paid remote work using that expertise.
notFitIf: You do not use assistive technology or need guaranteed monthly hours.
